## Overview



## Claims



## Validation
### Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` (HF cache, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`) |
| Frontend | `vllm-bench mm-processor` @ branch `rust-shm-mm-cache` |

### Method

Four runs share identical dataset parameters; each request carries one random
JPEG image (buckets `{(256,256,1): 0.5, (720,1280,1): 0.5}`) plus a 512-token
text prompt, 128 output tokens, serial submission (`--max-concurrency 1`), 20
measured prompts after 2 warmups, seed 42.

| Run | Flags | What it measures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — baseline | (no cache) | current behavior without the cache |
| B — cache miss | `--mm-processor-cache-type shm` | every item is a miss: put overhead |
| C — hash hit | B + `--random-mm-share-image` | identical image bytes per bucket; content-hash hits skip preprocessing, fetch/decode still runs |
| D — uuid hit | C + `--random-mm-share-image-uuid` | content parts carry a stable UUID; UUID hits skip fetch, decode, and preprocessing |

Warmup uses the same shared bucket images, so measured batches start with a
warm cache (100% hits in C and D).

### Results (mean / median, ms)

| Stage | A baseline | B cache miss | C hash hit | D uuid hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media_fetch` (base64 + JPEG decode) | 11.46 / 1.82 | 11.31 / 2.03 | 11.28 / 1.78 | **1.14 / 0.00** |
| `preprocess_image` (vision processor) | 2.37 / 0.80 | 3.82 / 1.00 | **0.41 / 0.01** | **0.36 / 0.00** |
| `preprocessor_total` (frontend mm total) | 13.85 / 2.57 | 15.16 / 2.88 | 11.70 / 1.82 | **1.52 / 0.03** |
| end-to-end mean | 416.6 | 421.2 | 394.8 | **384.3** |
| end-to-end p50 | 397.1 | 396.6 | 376.4 | **374.8** |
| end-to-end p99 | 466.5 | 523.4 | 461.1 | **455.4** |

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+//! Shared-memory multimodal processor cache (`--mm-processor-cache-type shm`).
+//!
+//! The frontend process (P0, single writer) owns a POSIX shm ring buffer; the
+//! engine's worker processes (P1) are the readers. On a cache miss the
+//! frontend stores the preprocessed [`MmKwargsItem`] in shm and sends the
+//! engine a tiny "address item" instead; on a hit it skips re-sending the
+//! data entirely. Oversize objects or a full buffer fall back to sending the
+//! full item inline.
+//!
+//! Rust port of the Python originals:
+//! - `SingleWriterShmRingBuffer` / `SingleWriterShmObjectStorage` /
+//!   `MsgpackSerde` from
+//!   `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_object_storage.py`
+//! - `ShmObjectStoreSenderCache` from `vllm/multimodal/cache/shm.py`
+//!
+//! [`MmKwargsItem`]: vllm_engine_core_client::protocol::multimodal::MmKwargsItem
+
+mod error;
+mod sender;
+mod serde;
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests;
+
+pub use error::{Error, Result};
+pub use sender::{MmProcessorShmCache, MmShmCacheConfig};

+#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+# /// script
+# requires-python = ">=3.11"
+# dependencies = [
+#   "msgpack>=1,<2",
+# ]
+# ///
+"""Validate a shm chunk written by the Rust `MmProcessorShmCache`.
+
+Reads the chunk at the given address out of the POSIX shm segment, verifies
+the HMAC handle signature against the 32-byte secret at the segment start,
+and msgpack-decodes the marker-prefixed body like the Python receiver's
+`MsgpackSerde.deserialize` would.
+"""
+
+import hashlib
+import hmac
+import mmap
+import struct
+import sys
+
+import msgpack
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    shm_path, address, monotonic_id, buffer_size, key, sig_hex = (
+        sys.argv[1],
+        int(sys.argv[2]),
+        int(sys.argv[3]),
+        int(sys.argv[4]),
+        sys.argv[5],
+        sys.argv[6],
+    )
+
+    with open(shm_path, "rb") as f:
+        buf = mmap.mmap(f.fileno(), 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ)
+
+    secret = bytes(buf[:32])
+
+    # signature = HMAC_SHA256(secret, sha256(key) + address_le8 + id_le4)
+    def sign(k: str) -> bytes:
+        payload = (
+            hashlib.sha256(k.encode("utf-8")).digest()
+            + address.to_bytes(8, "little")
+            + monotonic_id.to_bytes(4, "little")
+        )
+        return hmac.new(secret, payload, hashlib.sha256).digest()
+
+    signature = bytes.fromhex(sig_hex)
+    assert hmac.compare_digest(signature, sign(key)), "handle signature mismatch"
+    assert not hmac.compare_digest(signature, sign("other-key")), "wrong key verified"
+
+    offset = 32 + address % buffer_size
+    chunk_id, chunk_size = struct.unpack_from("<ii", buf, offset)
+    assert chunk_id == monotonic_id, (chunk_id, monotonic_id)
+    # `size` includes the 8-byte header.
+    assert chunk_size > 8
+
+    payload = buf[offset + 8 : offset + chunk_size]
+    (reader_count,) = struct.unpack_from("<i", payload, 0)
+    assert reader_count == 0, reader_count
+    # Format marker 0x01: the rest is one raw msgpack body.
+    assert payload[4] == 0x01, hex(payload[4])
+    body = payload[5:]
+
+    def ext_hook(code: int, data: bytes):
+        assert code == 3, f"unexpected ext type {code}"
+        return ("raw_view", data)
+
+    item = msgpack.unpackb(body, ext_hook=ext_hook, strict_map_key=False)
+    assert set(item) == {"offset", "pixel_values", "small"}, sorted(item)
+
+    for key, elem in item.items():
+        assert elem["field"] == ["batched", {"keep_on_cpu": False}], (key, elem)
+
+    assert item["offset"]["data"] == 7
+
+    dtype, shape, raw_view = item["pixel_values"]["data"]
+    assert dtype == "float32", dtype
+    assert shape == [128], shape
+    assert raw_view == ("raw_view", struct.pack("<128f", *range(128)))
+
+    dtype, shape, raw_view = item["small"]["data"]
+    assert dtype == "float32", dtype
+    assert shape == [2], shape
+    assert raw_view == ("raw_view", struct.pack("<2f", 1.0, 2.0))
+
+    print("OK")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+class TestMsgpackSerdeMarkerFormat(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Format-marker payloads written by the Rust frontend's shm cache."""
+
+    def test_deserialize_marker_prefixed_msgpack_body(self):
+        """A payload starting with 0x01 decodes as a raw msgpack body."""
+        serde = MsgpackSerde()
+        value = _dummy_item({"field1": 10, "field2": 20})
+
+        # All tensors are small, so they stay inline as ext type 3 raw views.
+        (body,) = serde.encoder.encode(value)
+        payload = b"\x01" + bytes(body)
+
+        result = serde.deserialize(memoryview(payload))
+        self.assertEqual(result, value)
+
+    def test_deserialize_legacy_pickle_format_unchanged(self):
+        """Legacy payloads start with \\x80 (pickle PROTO), not the marker."""
+        serde = MsgpackSerde()
+        value = _dummy_item({"field1": 10})
+        frames, _, metadata, _ = serde.serialize(value)
+        payload = metadata + b"".join(bytes(frame) for frame in frames)
+        self.assertEqual(payload[0], 0x80)
+
+        result = serde.deserialize(memoryview(payload))
+        self.assertEqual(result, value)
+

         return value, nbytes, serialized_metadata, len(serialized_metadata)
 
     def deserialize(self, data_view: memoryview) -> Any:
+        # Format marker 0x01: the rest of the payload is a single raw msgpack
+        # body encoding a MultiModalKwargsItem with all tensors inline as ext
+        # type 3 raw views (written by the Rust frontend's shm cache). Pickle
+        # protocol >= 2 streams always start with \x80 (PROTO), so the marker
+        # byte is unambiguous against the legacy format below.
+        if data_view[0] == 0x01:
+            return self.mm_decoder.decode([data_view[1:]])
+
